title: Continuous High-resolution Microscopic Observation of Replicative Aging in Budding Yeast
protocol: Produce silicon wafer molds by soft lithography for creating microfluidic chips.
Perform two-step photolithography using negative photoresist, SU-87.
Generate cell trapping area with the bottom layer of SU-8 2002 (height 3-4 μm).
Create channels with the top layer of SU-8 2010 (height 10 μm).
Cut one piece of Tough-Tag into thin strips of about 0.5 mm by 3 mm with a scalpel.
Place the strips carefully on the wafer slightly on top of the channel structure between the inlet channels and the micropad array.
Cover the glass Petri dish with a double layer of aluminum foil.
Put the wafer in the Petri dish.
Place an empty plastic cup on the balance.
Tare the balance.
Pour 40 g PDMS base into the plastic cup.
Add PDMS curing agent with a disposable pipette in a w/w ratio of 1:10, i.e., about 4 ml.
Mix PDMS and curing agent thoroughly for several minutes.
Pour the mixed PDMS onto the wafer in a glass Petri dish.
Place the Petri dish containing the wafer with PDMS into a desiccator connected to a vacuum pump to degas for about 30 min.
Polymerize the PDMS by placing the Petri dish on a hot plate at 120 °C for 1 hour, followed by another hour at 65 °C.
Remove the aluminum foil and polymerized PDMS from the glass Petri dish along with the wafer.
Peel off the aluminum foil and any thin residual layer of polymerized PDMS from the back of the wafer.
Lift up the PDMS layer carefully to separate it from the wafer.
Place the PDMS layer upside down on the bench, with channels facing up.
Cut out single chip designs imprinted on the PDMS carefully using a scalpel.
Retain about 3 mm of PDMS around the edges of the channels.
Punch holes in the PDMS at the ends of the inlet, outlet, and side channel by pushing a 20 Gauge Luer stub all the way through the PDMS.
Ensure the PDMS chip is lying upside down on the bench while punching the holes.
Remove any column of PDMS left behind in the Luer stub with tweezers before pulling the stub out.
Clean dust particles and residual PDMS from the surfaces of the chip using scotch tape.
Clean the cover glass to which the chip will be attached using scotch tape.
Place the cleaned chip and cover glass below the UV lamp of the Benchtop UV-Ozone Cleaner.
Expose the PDMS and cover glass to UV light for 6-8 minutes.
Immediately place the exposed surfaces of the PDMS chip on top of the cover glass after UV exposure.
Gently tap around the sides of the chip to promote attachment of the PDMS to the cover glass.
Tap gently to remove any air bubbles between the PDMS and cover glass.
Place the microfluidic setup on a hot plate at 100 °C for 60 min.
Test the bonding between the cover glass and PDMS chip by lifting the edges of the PDMS chip slightly.
Seal the sides of the chip where the PDMS meets the glass with nail polish or epoxy glue to prevent leakage.
Use a metal holder to secure the microfluidic chip, placing silicone gel between the glass and metal parts for a waterproof seal.
Screw nuts gently onto the metal holder to secure it without breaking the glass.
Connect thin tubes to the side channel and outlet channel of the chip using tweezers to insert the tubing in the punched holes.
Fill a 50 ml Luer-Lok syringe with culture medium.
Remove the air from the syringe and connect it sequentially to a syringe filter, a 20 Gauge Luer stub, a short thick tube (ca. 2 cm long), and a thin tube.
Place the syringe in the syringe pump.
Fast forward the pump until the thin tube is completely filled with medium.
Push the thin tube connected to the syringe into the inlet channel of the chip.
Let the medium flow through the chip at 10 μl/min.
Collect the medium leaving the chip (e.g., in a Petri dish).
Connect a 5 ml Luer tip syringe to a 20 Gauge Luer stub and a thick tube (ca. 3 cm).
Take a sample of the cell culture to be loaded into the chip.
Dilute cultures if necessary to achieve a cell count between 1-5 x 10^6 cells per ml.
Wash and resuspend cells in minimal medium with similar glucose percentage for improved loading efficiency when culturing on YPD.
Load approximately 1 ml of the cell suspension into the syringe.
Remove all air from the syringe.
Decrease the flow rate of the syringe pump to 0.5 μl/min.
Connect the syringe containing the cell suspension to the tube of the outlet channel.
Press the plunger gently to load cells, observing their settling underneath the micropads via ocular or computer screen.
Maintain pressure on the plunger until sufficient cells settle underneath the pads (optimum is 1-3 cells per pad).
Disconnect the syringe used for cell loading from the thin tubing of the outlet channel.
Flush the side channel for a couple of minutes at higher flow rates (10 μl/min) to remove air bubbles and/or cells that did not yet exit the chip.
Put the flow of the syringe pump back down to 0.5 μl/min.
Close the side channel off by connecting it to a thick tube containing a catheter plug at its end.
Increase the flow rate to 1-5 μl/min.
Start a movie with microscope and camera settings suitable for the experimental goal.
Set the microscope stage speed low enough that oil can follow its movement.
Image cells every 10 min for replicative lifespan determination.
Place an additional UV filter in the light path during DIC acquisition.
Image cells less frequently (e.g., every 20 min) when using fluorescence microscopy to avoid phototoxic effects.
Check the focus of images regularly throughout the experiment and adjust if necessary.
Complete the experiment when all initially loaded cells are dead, which typically takes up to 5 days.
